clue.text: Return smartly

parts.note: to return a remark smartly is to give a cheeky retort to someone in authority

explanation.definitionFit: A cheeky, quick verbal retort to a parent or teacher is a smart return of words.

clue.text: Plot shows Biblical character in mental upset

indicators.note: in places the Biblical man inside the rearranged letters of mental
upset means the letters of mental are knocked into a new order

parts.note: Lot is Abraham's nephew in Genesis, whose wife became a pillar of salt

explanation.surface: Someone is upset in mind by a figure from the Bible and shows it in a garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a story line but is a patch of land: an ALLOTMENT is a rented plot for growing vegetables in Britain. 'upset' makes ALMENT, and 'in' places the man inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rented patch of municipal ground for growing vegetables is a garden plot.

clue.text: Type in forename

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Type in forename' with no letter count; no parse of these words gives the answer, so the clue looks cut short in the OCR.

clue.text: Time's original entirety?

indicators.note: original as in creative or inventive, so the letters of entirety are made into something new

explanation.surface: A question whether the original meaning of time is its entire span.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' is an unusual anagram signal: it asks for an inventive rearrangement of ENTIRETY. The 's after Time is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Endless duration with no beginning or end is time without limit.

clue.text: Eats, Shoots & Leaves going fast

parts.note: each of the three verbs in the punctuation book's title has a single synonym meaning to do it hurriedly: gobble food, run up to seed, dash off

explanation.surface: The punctuation guide Eats, Shoots & Leaves is selling quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Eats, Shoots & Leaves is a bestselling book about punctuation. One verb covers all three done in haste: to gulp food, for a plant to run to seed, and to run off.
explanation.definitionFit: Gulping food, a plant running to seed and running away are all senses of the same verb of sudden haste.

clue.text: Burn like car without wife?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Burn like car without wife?': the answer looks like crewmate less W, but no reading of 'like car' gives CREWMATE, so a word seems misread in the OCR.

clue.text: Those lagging behind in division?

parts.note: a league division splits into an upper and a lower part, and the teams trailing are in the lower part

explanation.definitionFit: The lower section of a league table holds the teams trailing behind.

clue.text: Where one stays following this

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a place where one stays put: in this spot, carrying on
a formal word for after this point, from now

explanation.definitionFit: Formal legal English uses the word for after this point, and as two words it means staying in this place.

clue.text: Deliveries, left arm mostly, get shorter and too wide?

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word arm is kept, dropping its last letter
shorter means the word get is cut, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A left-arm bowler's overs get shorter and too wide, a cricket report.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls; a wide is a ball bowled out of reach. 'mostly' cuts ARM to AR and 'shorter' cuts GET to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something excessively big or oversized is too wide, with the question mark nodding to a cricket wide.

clue.text: Substitute in position with United

parts.note: the lie of the land is its position or layout
U is the usual abbreviation for United in football team names

explanation.surface: A substitute comes into position alongside Manchester United, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'with' are links. The definition rests on the phrase 'in lieu of', meaning in place of, as a substitute for.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for place survives in the phrase meaning as a replacement for, so it stands for a substitute.

clue.text: Get annoyed in attempt to arrive at agreement

indicators.note: in puts the word for getting annoyed inside the word for attempt

parts.note: an attempt is a try
eat is used as in 'what's eating you?', so to be eaten up is to get annoyed

explanation.surface: Someone gets cross during an effort to reach a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the eating word inside the attempt. 'to arrive at' is a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal pact signed between nations is an agreement.

clue.text: Desk tidy of pens, etc?

parts.note: a desk tidy is an office stand for holding writing kit, here pens with their ink bottles

explanation.definitionFit: A stand on a desk holding ink bottles and pens is a tidy for writing equipment.

clue.text: Stunning one, Listener grid set up to daunt

parts.note: a dish is slang for a strikingly attractive person
the ear is the organ that listens

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word for grid is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a net is a mesh or grid

explanation.surface: A dazzling solver finds the Listener crossword grid set up to intimidate.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is a famously hard crossword in The Times, but here it is just the EAR. 'set up' turns NET into TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage someone or sap their courage is to daunt them.

clue.text: Address more than one's behaviour

definitions.meaning: address in the sense of bearing, the way someone conducts themselves
behaviour or etiquette is this word in the plural, so one of them is the singular

explanation.surface: A speech about several people's conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's bearing or style is their address, and good conduct is the plural of the same word.

clue.text: They send you off the field

definitions.text: They send you off the field

parts.words: They send you off the field
parts.note: sounds like referees dismissing players, but means the officials who fire the gun to begin a race

explanation.definitionFit: Officials who signal the beginning of a race send the field of runners away.

clue.text: Promotion hampered by red tape, sadly, must be modified again

indicators.note: hampered by means the word for promotion is hemmed in by the rearranged red tape
sadly signals that the letters of red tape go wrong and are rearranged

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a promotion

explanation.surface: A marketing campaign held up by bureaucracy has to be changed again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' makes REAPTED, and 'hampered by' places the promotion inside it. 'must be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjusted once more for new conditions means changed or modified again.

clue.text: Bound to stop, having been round

indicators.note: round means the word been surrounds the word for stop

parts.note: to hold is to stop or halt, as in 'hold it!'

explanation.surface: Someone is bound to stop after having been round the block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' places the stop inside the other word. 'to' and 'having' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Obliged or indebted to someone means morally bound to them.

clue.text: 24, say, in a to-do

parts.note: the answer to 24 down, read as two words, is a wager, and a small one is called a flutter in British slang
flutter is British slang for a small bet

explanation.surface: Something from clue 24 causes a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 24 down read as 'a bet'; 'say' means an equivalent, so 'a bet' becomes A FLUTTER, a flutter being British slang for a modest wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitated and nervously excited, as one is when caught up in a commotion or fuss.

clue.text: Lied for the rest?

parts.note: a Lied is a German art song, and a song to help someone rest is one sung to a child at bedtime

explanation.definitionFit: A gentle song sung to send a child to sleep is a song for rest.

clue.text: Awkward age, wandering round a lot, leaderless

indicators.note: round means the rearranged age goes round the shortened word for a lot
wandering means the letters of age stray into a new order
leaderless means the word for a lot loses its first letter

parts.note: much means a lot

explanation.surface: An awkward age spent wandering about a lot without a guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' makes GAE; 'leaderless' drops the first letter of the word for a lot; 'round' wraps the first around the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Socially clumsy and lacking grace is awkward.

clue.text: Prompting in a line waiting to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard means the word for standing in line is said out loud and gives a word that sounds the same

parts.note: waiting in a line is queuing

explanation.surface: A prompter is waiting in line for their turn to be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: QUEUING, standing in line, sounds the same as the word for giving actors their prompts.
explanation.definitionFit: In the theatre, giving an actor the signal for their line is prompting them.

clue.text: Ample time in concession period

parts.note: full means ample or plentiful

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for time inside the word for concession

parts.note: a sop is a concession made to placate someone

explanation.surface: Plenty of time is given during a period of concessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the time inside the concession. 'period' is the American name for the dot that ends a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation dot ending a sentence is called a period in American English.

clue.text: Is toothbrush to be found in drugstore?

parts.note: is shortens to 's, as in it's
a toothbrush moustache is a small clipped one, and tash is British slang for a moustache

explanation.surface: A question whether a toothbrush can be bought at a chemist's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toothbrush' is the short clipped moustache, and TASH is British slang for a moustache. 'to be found in' is a link; a drugstore read cryptically is a store of drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden hoard of illicit substances is a store of drugs.

clue.text: Path bringing you to eastern peninsula, some say

indicators.note: some say means the name of the country is spoken aloud and gives a word sounding like it to some speakers

parts.note: Korea is a peninsula in East Asia

explanation.surface: A route that leads you to an Asian peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent KOREA and the answer sound alike, hence 'some say'. 'bringing you to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's progress through working life is their professional path.

clue.text: Further 17, say

parts.note: the answer to 17 across opens with a, kept as it is
a flutter is British slang for a small wager, so the rest of 17 across stands for a wager

explanation.surface: More of the same as clue 17.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 across is A FLUTTER; 'say' signals an equivalent, and a flutter is British slang for a small wager, so A FLUTTER becomes A BET.
explanation.definitionFit: To support or encourage, often a crime, is to further it.

clue.text: One shortly to fall in battle?

definitions.text: One shortly to fall in battle?

parts.words: One shortly to fall in battle?
parts.note: sounds like a doomed soldier, but means an airborne soldier, named in short form, who drops from an aircraft into battle under a canopy

explanation.definitionFit: An airborne soldier, abbreviated, drops from an aircraft into combat.

clue.text: Be taunted, perhaps, as one coming out

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of be taunted could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone may be mocked as they come out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' is the formal entry of a young woman into society, not a declaration of identity.
explanation.definitionFit: A young woman making her formal entry into high society is said to come out.

clue.text: Like bed-hopper, with any depth he panicked

indicators.note: panicked means the letters of any depth he are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone panicked at a promiscuous partner, in any depth of feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: The word bed-hopper contains a dash joining bed and hopper, so it is literally joined by a dash.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound joined by a dash between its parts is written with a dash, as bed-hopper is.
